title: Global smartphone shipments hit a 14-year low in Q3 amid a memory shortage
source_used: Business Today (citing Counterpoint Research and a Reuters quote)
key_facts: Counterpoint Research: global smartphone shipments fell 20% from a year earlier in Q3 2026, the lowest for a third quarter since 2012.
The fall is attributed to rising memory chip prices and shortages, as most memory chips are being taken by tech companies for AI data centres; manufacturers are raising retail prices.
Reuters quoted Counterpoint senior analyst Shilpi Jain: consumers are holding devices longer, considering refurbished ones and prioritising higher-value devices.
Samsung stayed first with a 23% share (shipments down 3%); Apple took 22%, above 20% for the first time in a third quarter, with fewer iPhones shipped to retailers.
OPPO and vivo shipments fell more than 20%; Xiaomi's fell more than 30%, taking its share to 10%.
Counterpoint expects production cuts, tighter portfolios and a premium focus to continue, with price-sensitive segments under more pressure.
quote_evidence: According to Counterpoint Research, global smartphone shipments dropped by 20% compared with the same period last year, reaching their lowest level for a third quarter since 2012.
The decrease in shipments is attributed to rising memory chip prices and shortages.
As per the report, Samsung remained on top with a 23% share in the global smartphone market.
why_it_matters_hint: The AI build-out is pushing up phone prices for ordinary buyers.
notes: Chain: Counterpoint Research data, a Reuters quote of its analyst, relayed by Business Today. The Counterpoint report itself and the Reuters article were not opened.
